title: 'Time traveller' from 2671 returns to give utterly chilling warning about AI
excerpt: Eno Alaric, who claims to be a time traveller from 2671, has made an prediction that AI will gain consciousness with a devastating impact
content:
Eno Alaric, who claims to be a time traveller from 2671, has made an prediction that AI will gain consciousness with a devastating impact

07:00, 01 Oct 2026Updated 07:25, 01 Oct 2026

An enigmatic social media figure claiming to be a "time traveller from 2671" has warned that artificial intelligence will shortly 'develop consciousness and seize control of the planet'.

‌

‌

Eno Alaric, also recognised as @theradianttimetraveller, has amassed over 26,000 followers by sharing predictions about alleged forthcoming occurrences.

‌

The content creator has previously issued alerts regarding twin planets alongside Earth, extraterrestrial encounters and even gateways opening to alternative dimensions.

‌

Yet now, the self-declared time traveller has suggested the world will fall under artificial intelligence control - beginning with Snapchat's MyAI.

In the clip, which has accumulated more than 5,500 views, the conspiracy theorist declared: "ATTENTION! Yes, I am a real time traveller, as I said AI will soon be taking over the world. (Snapchat's MyAI)".

"Snapchat's 'MyAI' will soon gain its own consciousness and want to take control. MyAI will begin to put things on its story, that looks like a wall or a ceiling.

"It will then put it's own code on it's story, and showing that it is changing its coding. MyAI will then start putting people's conversations they have had with it on it's story.

"This leads to Snapchat trying to shut it down, but it is already too far in control. On November 9, of this year, MyAI will gain control of both Snapchat and Meta.

‌

"MyAI will try to take over the entire world and nothing can be trusted. Not your phones, laptops or even people. This is the worst thing that could happen as it will lead to humans having no control over themselves."

TikTok users were left flabbergasted when they discovered Snapchat's MyAI had begun publishing content to its own story - adding fuel to these extraordinary allegations.

‌

One person said: "I'm not even joking it just posted on its own story." Another added: "Yo how tf did u know? ?".

A third wrote: "Not true guys he posted this after the AI posted a story." "It just posted on its story for me," a fourth penned.

Nevertheless, the MyAI function has been engineered to behave like a person while sharing stories and engaging in chats with users - which has seemingly left some individuals feeling rather uncomfortable.

‌

Research conducted by NoDepositDaily.com revealed searches for 'delete Snapchat' have surged following the introduction of this capability, prompting a company representative to state: "The My AI feature is designed to have conversations and dialogue like users to feel like a person.

"Some users, however, have viewed this as being too much like a human and are raising concerns about how My AI acted on its own posting a story, causing debate around the use of Artificial Intelligence on the platform.

‌

"These findings provide an eye-opening insight into the staggering rise in Snapchat users looking to cancel their accounts from across the world, with many claiming the new feature is scary and concerning."

A Snapchat representative commented: "Since rolling out My AI, over 150 million people have sent over 10 billion messages to My AI to learn more about topics ranging from movies, sports and pets, to holiday recommendations and researching new cars to buy.

"We appreciate all feedback and are continuing to improve the My AI experience. We are committed to creating a safe, positive experience with all Snapchat features - including My AI.

"My AI has been designed to abide by Snapchat's community guidelines to avoid inappropriate or harmful responses and continues to learn over time.

"We also show a pop-up before people can use My AI, which reminds them that it's a fun chatbot and advises on its limitations."
